headline: 729 dead in 110 days: Measles outbreak kills 5 more children in 24 hours
summary: The death toll from measles and measles-like symptoms has surged to 729 across Bangladesh, with five more children dying in a single day.
details: According to the latest report from the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), five children died within 24 hours due to measles or measles-like symptoms.
The deaths occurred across several regions, with two children in the Chattogram division and one each in Dhaka, Rangpur, and Sylhet divisions.
In the last 24 hours alone, 968 suspected measles cases were reported, and 851 children were admitted to hospitals, with 301 of them in the Dhaka division.
Over the past 110 days, the total number of deaths has reached 729. This includes 636 deaths due to measles-like symptoms and 93 confirmed measles deaths.
Since the first case was detected on March 15, a total of 103,961 people have been affected by the disease, with 87,262 requiring hospitalization.
Of the total cases, 12,425 have been confirmed as measles, while 83,543 patients have been discharged from hospitals over the 110-day period.
caption:
729 deaths in just 110 days. Five more children lost to measles in the last 24 hours.

According to the latest report from the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), five children died within 24 hours due to measles or measles-like symptoms.

The deaths occurred across several regions, with two children in the Chattogram division and one each in Dhaka, Rangpur, and Sylhet divisions.

In the last 24 hours alone, 968 suspected measles cases were reported, and 851 children were admitted to hospitals, with 301 of them in the Dhaka division.

Over the past 110 days, the total number of deaths has reached 729. This includes 636 deaths due to measles-like symptoms and 93 confirmed measles deaths.

Since the first case was detected on March 15, a total of 103,961 people have been affected by the disease, with 87,262 requiring hospitalization.

Of the total cases, 12,425 have been confirmed as measles, while 83,543 patients have been discharged from hospitals over the 110-day period.

headline_marked: Messi's Argentina to face [[Cape Verde in World Cup]] knockout stage
headline: Messi's Argentina to face Cape Verde in World Cup knockout stage
summary: The defending champions face the tournament's biggest surprise, the smallest nation ever to reach the knockout rounds.
details: Defending champions Argentina will face debutants Cape Verde in a Round-of-32 meeting in Miami on Saturday. This matchup has become one of the tournament's most captivating ties after a surprising group stage.

Cape Verde, the smallest nation to reach the knockout stage, defied predictions by drawing with Spain, Uruguay, and Saudi Arabia. They have completed a remarkable 'fairytale' run to become the smallest country ever to reach the FIFA World Cup knockout rounds.

Lionel Messi, the tournament's joint-leading scorer with six goals in three matches, will lead Argentina. The spotlight remains on the captain as he pursues back-to-back world titles in his sixth World Cup.

A key duel will be between Messi and Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha, who has kept two clean sheets. Argentina's offense has scored in every match and every half of their opening games, but they rely heavily on Messi for their goals.

Argentina's coach Lionel Scaloni is expected to restore the side that beat Austria, with potential returns for Nicolas Tagliafico and Cristian Romero. Lautaro Martinez may start ahead of Julian Alvarez due to recent form.

Cape Verde, ranked 64th in the world, is looking for another famous upset. With Morocco already in the Round of 16, they now carry the hopes of African football as they seek to continue their fairytale run.
caption:
A fairytale run meets a global icon. Can the smallest nation in World Cup history reach a knockout upset?

Defending champions Argentina will face debutants Cape Verde in a Round-of-32 meeting in Miami on Saturday. This matchup has become one of the tournament's most captivating ties after a surprising group stage.

Cape Verde, the smallest nation to reach the knockout stage, defied predictions by drawing with Spain, Uruguay, and Saudi Arabia. They have completed a remarkable 'fairytale' run to become the smallest country ever to reach the FIFA World Cup knockout rounds.

Lionel Messi, the tournament's joint-leading scorer with six goals in three matches, will lead Argentina. The spotlight remains on the captain as he pursues back-to-back world titles in his sixth World Cup.

A key duel will be between Messi and Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha, who has kept two clean sheets. Argentina's offense has scored in every match and every half of their opening games, but they rely heavily on Messi for their goals.

Argentina's coach Lionel Scaloni is expected to restore the side that beat Austria, with potential returns for Nicolas Tagliafico and Cristian Romero. Lautaro Martinez may start ahead of Julian Alvarez due to recent form.

Cape Verde, ranked 64th in the world, is looking for another famous upset. With Morocco already in the Round of 16, they now carry the hopes of African football as they seek to continue their fairytale run.
